library_preparation_preflight.summary: videoinput wraps a Windows-only DirectShow webcam-capture library (ofTheo/videoInput); Maven Central ships only windows-x86/windows-x86_64 native classifiers for 0.200-1.5.9, so no dependency, Docker image, or env var can make native calls succeed on this repo's Linux CI.
library_preparation_preflight.agent_guidance: Do not expect the normal testRuntimeOnly "org.bytedeco:videoinput-platform:$libraryVersion" scaffold to provide a usable native library here — that -platform POM only resolves to windows-x86/windows-x86_64 artifacts, none of which load on the ubuntu-22.04/ubuntu-latest runners this repo uses. Any test path that actually calls into the native videoInput API (enumerating capture devices, opening a device, grabbing a frame) will throw UnsatisfiedLinkError or org.bytedeco.javacpp.Loader$UnsupportedPlatformException at both javaTest and nativeTest time, independent of setup. Meaningful reachability coverage is likely limited to Java-side code that doesn't trigger native loading (e.g. constant/enum classes, configuration objects, pure-Java helper methods) — tests should be designed to avoid asserting real capture behavior, or to explicitly expect/catch the unsupported-platform failure rather than treat it as a bug to fix.
risks: The underlying videoInput library is Windows-only by design (DirectShow-based); this is a platform constraint of the upstream project, not a missing build-setup gap, so no combination of dependency/docker_image/env setup resolves it.

If the generated tests cannot exercise any meaningful native-backed behavior on Linux, this issue may be better resolved by flagging it back for human review (e.g. accept Java-only reachability scope, or decide the library is out of scope for this Linux-CI-based repository) rather than proceeding as a normal new-library addition.
